title: Financial Crises and the Authority's Role
summary: How firms and markets fail, the roles of the supervisor, resolution authority, central bank and protection schemes, and how an authority organises itself to take crisis decisions.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How firms and markets fail, the roles of the supervisor, resolution authority, central bank and protection schemes, and how an authority organises itself to take crisis decisions.
Learning Objectives: Explain the common paths from stress to failure
Describe the roles of the authorities involved in a crisis
Assess the authority's own crisis governance and readiness
Syllabus: Anatomy of firm failure: solvency, liquidity, conduct and operational triggers
Supervisors, resolution authorities, central banks and protection schemes
FSB Key Attributes and IADI principles
Crisis governance: decision rights, playbooks and escalation within the authority
Intended Audience: Supervisors and risk specialists responsible for firms that may come under stress
Resolution, financial stability and macroprudential staff
Senior managers and executives who would lead or take decisions in the authority's crisis response
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervision, financial stability or risk work is helpful. No prior crisis or resolution experience is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
Basel Committee, Guidelines for Identifying and Dealing with Weak Banks (2015)
IADI, Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems
